text:
Registered sales volume reached 14,432 units valued at AED 42,635,071,625 in the last four weeks, representing a 41.5 percent increase compared to the previous period. Mortgage registrations totaled 5,985, which are recorded separately from sales transactions. The off-plan share of sales stood at 57.7 percent, slightly lower than the 59.4 percent recorded in the prior four weeks.

The median residential price per square foot rose to AED 1,689, a 1.4 percent increase from AED 1,665 in the previous period. Top selling areas by volume over twelve weeks include Dubai South with 3,396 sales and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,498 sales. Dubai Creek Harbour showed the strongest price momentum among major areas with a 7.9 percent increase in median price per square foot over twelve weeks.

Rental activity remained robust with 110,328 contracts registered, where 51.6 percent were renewals. The median annual residential rent was AED 68,729. Estimated gross yields for flats were highest in Zaabeel First at 9.0 percent and International City Phase 1 at 8.6 percent. Town Square followed with a 7.0 percent yield, while Dubai Sports City and Dubai Production City recorded yields of 6.7 percent and 6.4 percent respectively.

Areas showing significant price heating include Al Yufrah 1 with a 41.8 percent twelve-week price increase and Dubai Industrial City at 10.2 percent. Conversely, Palm Jumeirah cooled by 16.7 percent and Jumeirah Lakes Towers by 15.3 percent over the same period. The anomaly monitor flagged 926 residential sales in the last 60 days priced more than 35 percent away from their comparable cell median. These figures are based on registered DLD data and Ejari contracts using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals and outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
